{"id":"PKIX-9bzr","title":"Finish the mutation sweep across the remaining crates","description":"## Why

pkix-path's sweep: 552 mutants, 100 missed, 393 caught, 53 unviable, 6 timeouts. The survivors found real defects, not just missing tests -- including a §4.2.1.10 rule enforced on intermediates and on neither trust-anchor constructor.

On that hit rate this is the cheapest remaining source of findings in the workspace.

## Status

RUNNING as of 2026-11-27. pkix-revocation (276 mutants), pkix-chain (205), pkix-identity (164). Output under the session scratchpad, mutants-<crate>/.

## Method, which matters for reading the results

* WITHOUT -D warnings. A mutant that trips an unused-binding warning is reported unviable rather than as a survivor, which hides real gaps -- the automated form of a false negative that bit this session four times by hand.
* --timeout-multiplier 4, so a slow-but-correct test is not mistaken for a hang.
* Triage by 'is this a bug', not by category. A survivor in a public helper unused inside its own crate (cert_is_ca, tbs_certificate_der) is invisible to a crate-scoped sweep by construction -- consumers may cover it, and that needs checking per case rather than assuming either way.

## Still unswept after these three

pkix-ct, pkix-lint, pkix-ac, pkix-dane, pkix-mta-sts, pkix-revocation-http, pkix-truststore and the rest.","status":"open","priority":1,"issue_type":"task","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-27T08:00:31.302940196Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-27T08:00:31.302940196Z"}

{"notes":"## Result, 2026-11-27

All three sweeps complete. 90 survivors closed, each mutation re-applied by
hand afterwards to confirm it now fails.

    crate             mutants  missed  closed  left
    pkix-revocation       276      93      50    43
    pkix-chain            205      16      15     1
    pkix-identity         164      27      19     8

pkix-chain's number is from a re-run with --all-features. The first run used
default features and reported 38, of which 22 were spurious -- see below.

## Two build defects the sweeps found before testing anything

pkix-revocation tested ZERO mutants on the first attempt: cargo-mutants
refuses a tree whose baseline build fails, and
`cargo test -p pkix-revocation` did not compile. Three CRL test targets
imported `crl`-gated items with no `[[test]] required-features`. CI passed
because `cargo test --workspace` resolves features once for the whole graph
and pkix-difftest enables `crl`. Fixed in fe1e6012; the CI step that catches
the class is 3b152d8a.

Then `--features crl` alone did not compile either: the signer_discovery test
module needs `std::fs` and `format!`, and `crl` stopped implying `std` when
no_std CRL checking became possible. Fixed in d59df224.

## Method correction: name the features

cargo-mutants builds its mutant list from the syntax tree, before `cfg` is
resolved, so code behind a feature the sweep did not enable is mutated
anyway, the mutation changes nothing, and the mutant is reported MISSED --
indistinguishable in the report from a real gap. The default-feature
pkix-chain run reported survivors in `combine_smtp_transport_security`,
`permits_delivery` and `verify_attribute_cert`, all behind off-by-default
features and all already tested under their own. Recorded in AGENTS.md
under "Name the features when running a mutation sweep".

Also check the baseline's Test phase duration in `outcomes.json`: a second
or two means almost nothing ran.

## Still unswept

pkix-ct, pkix-lint, pkix-ac, pkix-dane, pkix-mta-sts, pkix-revocation-http,
pkix-truststore, pkix-path-builder, pkix-profiles and the rest."}

{"notes":"## pkix-path, 2026-11-27 (evening)

verifiers.rs swept clean after the fixes: 68 mutants, 56 caught,
12 unviable, 0 missed, 0 timeouts. Scoped with -f '**/verifiers.rs'.

Full-crate sweep in progress. What the earlier attempts got wrong:

The crate's 541 mutants looked like a four-hour run at 76% I/O wait, and
that was self-inflicted. Three things were competing for the same disk --
hand-verification runs rebuilding the same crate, leftover
/data/tmp/cargo-mutants-PKIX-* trees from killed sweeps, and the sweep
itself. With nothing else running, verifiers.rs did 68 mutants in five
minutes, which puts 541 at roughly forty.

The real multiplier is the integration test count, not the mutant count:
pkix-path has thirty files in tests/, so each mutant relinks thirty
binaries before an assertion runs. Recorded in AGENTS.md (fb8ca3d3) with
the two levers -- -f to scope the mutants, -- to pass a --test or --lib
through to cargo test -- and the caveat that narrowing the tests narrows
what the result can claim.

## Still unswept

pkix-ct, pkix-lint, pkix-ac, pkix-dane, pkix-mta-sts,
pkix-revocation-http, pkix-truststore, pkix-path-builder, pkix-profiles.

Check each one's integration test count before estimating: that is what
sets the per-mutant cost."}

{"notes":"## pkix-ac, 2026-11-27 (evening)

157 mutants, 51s with -j 3. First sweep: 30 missed. Now 1, the
equivalent `|` -> `^` in `header`, noted at the site.

Six commits, every mutation hand-verified: 36d6c00a, d1c3c295, 883cf4ea,
8389612b, 3cb926a3, 47d4776b.

The crate had 2 integration test files for 2032 source lines, and the
survivors clustered in exactly the places that implies.

### Three RFC clauses with no fixture at all

§4.2.2's subjectAltName half -- "the entityName MUST be the same as the
PKC subject field OR ONE OF THE VALUES OF THE PKC subjectAltName field
extension". The borrowed holder certificate (pkix-ct's
precert-leaf-final) has no subjectAltName, so subject_alt_names could
have returned nothing whatever and the suite would pass.

§4.2.8's issuerUniqueID match. Nothing in the directory carried a
subjectUniqueID -- neither OpenSSL nor cryptography emits the field --
so only the (None, None) arm was reachable.

§4.2.2's baseCertificateID.issuerUID match. Same cause: the holder
certificate has no issuerUniqueID, so only the (None, _) arm ran.

### And one shape worth remembering

§6 forbids an AC carrying both noRevAvail and a revocation pointer.
Every fixture exercising that rule carries BOTH extensions -- and for
such an AC, "some extension is noRevAvail" and "some extension is not
noRevAvail" are both true. The fixtures that test the rule are precisely
the ones that cannot see how it is computed. An AC with a pointer and no
noRevAvail is the one that distinguishes them.

### Fixture notes

Re-running tests/fixtures/gen.py re-signs all 60-odd ACs with fresh
ECDSA nonces, so the whole directory shows modified for no change in
meaning. Restore everything but the genuinely new files. Noted in gen.py.

The two spliced certificates (make_unique_id.py) are re-signed with keys
the workspace already commits, and the splice leaves
subjectPublicKeyInfo alone -- so the authority's key is unchanged and
every AC signed with aa-key.pem still verifies, while the certificate
stays properly issued. The generator checks all of that before writing."}

{"notes":"## pkix-truststore, 2026-11-27 (evening)

58 mutants. First sweep: 25 missed, 19 caught of 44 viable -- the
thinnest coverage of any crate swept today. Re-sweep after b4fdcff7:
44 caught, 0 missed, 0 timeouts. Clean.

Three clusters, and the first is worth generalising.

### A lossy-by-design mapping fails silently by design too

io_error_kind_serde::deserialize maps nineteen ErrorKind names and sends
everything else to ErrorKind::Other. That is deliberate and documented:
a producer on a newer Rust emitting an unknown kind must still reach an
older consumer with its message intact.

The consequence is that deleting any one arm has exactly the same effect
as meeting an unknown kind -- degrade to Other, no error anywhere. Only
"NotFound" had a test, so eighteen arms could each have been deleted with
the suite green.

Two tests fix it, and both are needed. The wire names written out by hand
as the oracle, so an upstream Debug change surfaces as a failure rather
than a silently different wire format; AND an explicit assertion that an
unknown name degrades to Other with its message kept. Without the second,
a shim answering Other for everything is indistinguishable from one
missing a single arm.

Same template as pkix-revocation's crl_reason_serde.

### A documented boundary with no test at it

read_file_capped's rustdoc states the contract exactly -- cap + 1 is
requested from take so the read distinguishes "exactly cap bytes"
(accepted) from "more than cap bytes" (rejected). Two comparisons
implement it; every existing test was a 2 KiB file against a 1 KiB cap, a
thousand bytes from either edge. Read as >=, a bundle sized to the
documented public cap on purpose cannot load.

### Display and source, again

Same shape as pkix-path and pkix-revocation: no in-crate caller, and
rendering a load failure is the one thing a deployment reads when its
anchors do not appear.

## Status

    crate              mutants  missed  note
    pkix-path              541       1  equivalent (1 << 0), 5 timeouts
    pkix-ac                157       1  equivalent (| vs ^)
    pkix-truststore         58       0  clean

### pkix-profiles: 8 equivalent mutants

`policy_oids` returns `&[]`; the mutant returns `Vec::leak(Vec::new())`.
Both are empty slices and no caller can tell them apart. Verified rather
than assumed, and recorded at the trait impl. The 16 `version` mutants
are killed by a table of expected strings written out by hand.

### pkix-path-builder: signed_by is pruning, not a gate

This looked like the worst survivor of the day -- a builder that believes
every certificate is signed by every other -- and it is unobservable
through the public API:

- every candidate the iterator yields goes to validate_path, which makes
  the same signature decision again, and
- when the verifier-aware search yields nothing,
  build_first_valid_path_with_config falls back to a topology-only pass
  over the same pool so the caller still learns why the best candidate
  failed.

Both routes reach the same NoValidPath with the same error and the same
count. Only the number of candidates validated differs, and on success
that is not in the result. A test asserting "a bad-signature chain is
refused" passes either way and would tell a reader the builder's check
is what stops forged chains. It is not; validate_path is. Recorded at
the function.

### Two fixtures worth more than the mutants they killed

A cross-certified CA (pkix-path-builder/tests/fixtures/cross-certified):
two certificates naming one CA and carrying one key, one issued by the
anchor and one by a second authority. Needed because rank_candidates'
anchor preference was untestable twice over -- reaches_anchor is only
computed for signature-checked searches, and no fixture gave a leaf two
candidate issuers, so the sort had one element and any order was the
same order. Both routes validate and differ in length, which is how
order becomes observable. A bridge-PKI shape the crate had no test for.

An MTA-STS max_age pair: 0031557600 is ten digits parsing to exactly
MAX_AGE_LIMIT (in the grammar however large the value) and 00000000001 is
eleven digits parsing to 1 (outside it however small). Those two inputs
are the only ones that separate the length guard from the limit check
below it, since every other malformed value produces the same
InvalidMaxAge from either.

### A mistake worth not repeating

The first version of the mta-sts borrowed-store test called the methods
on a concrete `&Recording` and killed none of the seven mutants it was
named after: method resolution auto-derefs and reaches the inner store
directly, so `impl PolicyStore for &S` was never selected. Route the
calls through a generic `fn f<S: PolicyStore>(store: S)` and pass the
reference -- inside a generic the compiler has no concrete type to deref
through. pkix-path's verifier_forwarding.rs already did it that way and
I rebuilt the wrong version from scratch. The confirming sweep caught it;
hand-verification would not have, because I believed the test covered
the impl.

## Remaining

pkix-ct, pkix-lint, pkix-dane, pkix-revocation-http."}

{"notes":"## pkix-dane, 2026-11-27 (late)

237 mutants. First sweep 19 missed + 13 timeouts; now 1 missed
(equivalent, documented) + 13 timeouts (PKIX-1zkq, closed as accounted
for). Commit b01a7843.

Three findings bear on the standing constraint that a DANE failure must
stay distinguishable so messages can be tagged, routed or held:

- has_usable_record had only its positive direction tested, so it could
  answer true always. RFC 7671 §17 treats an all-unusable response as if
  no TLSA record were published -- which is "DANE does not apply here",
  not "the peer failed DANE". The two are what a sender routes on.
- matches_spki's `!is_usable() || selector != Spki` fails open as `&&`: a
  publication §17 says to ignore becomes a positive authentication
  result.
- mx_was_secure, came_from_mx and next_hop are only ever asserted false
  in the existing suite, taken from the insecure-MX and non-MX cases. All
  three could answer false, and next_hop "", with a secure MX delivery
  reported as an unauthenticated non-MX one to nowhere.

The NoMx arm (§2.2.2) is a second copy of the Mx arm's trust logic and had
no test at all -- five mutants, including a dropped negation that inverts
the rule into refusing only secure answers.

One test of mine was wrong and the code was right: I asserted next_hop()
returns the MX hostname. Its rustdoc says "the original next-hop domain,
before any CNAME expansion". Read the doc, fixed the expectation.

## pkix-ct, first sweep

452 mutants, 91 missed -- but 49 are Vec::with_capacity hint arithmetic on
four lines, equivalent by construction. See PKIX-t91v. The real set is 42:
6 at the RFC 6962 §3.2 ASN.1Cert length boundary, 4 at the 3-byte length
prefix's top octet, 3 in the Merkle proof depth, 17 in log_list.rs, 8 in
raw_der.rs, 2 elsewhere."}

{"notes":"## Campaign complete, 2026-11-27

Every crate swept. Final state, survivors all either killed or
documented at the code with the reason they must survive:

    crate                 mutants  first  final  note
    pkix-path                 541     18      1  equivalent 1<<0, +5 timeouts
    pkix-ac                   157     30      1  equivalent | vs ^
    pkix-truststore            58     25      0  clean
    pkix-mta-sts              122     14      0  clean
    pkix-profiles              72     24      8  all equivalent (policy_oids)
    pkix-path-builder          99     16      1  signed_by, pruning not a gate
    pkix-dane                 237     19      1  equivalent, +13 timeouts
    pkix-ct                   452     91     63  49 capacity hints + 14 docd
    pkix-lint                 671    104      8  equivalent + unreachable
    pkix-revocation-http      252     25      0  clean
    pkix-revocation           288     18     18  14 equivalent, 1 helper
    pkix-identity             164      3      3  all explained
    pkix-chain                  -      1      1  PKIX-zn4l, unobservable

The two biggest crates were swept by parallel agents in isolated
worktrees and merged after re-verification in the main tree.

## What the campaign was actually for

The recurring finding is not "this operator is wrong". It is that a test
can assert the right rule and still be blind to it. Six distinct forms
turned up, all now in AGENTS.md:

- A guard whose verdict a later check reproduces looks redundant. Ask
  whether the two compute the same expression (verify_inclusion_proof:
  yes, equivalent) or measure different things (max_age: no, and
  0031557600 against 00000000001 separates them).
- A rule naming a position needs a fixture that differs at that
  position. AllCertificatesSamePoliciesTest10 can try every policy
  combination and never see which certificate is checked.
- The fixture that demonstrates a rule often cannot test how it is
  decided. Every §6 fixture carries BOTH noRevAvail and a pointer, where
  the scan and its negation agree.
- A negative assertion is only evidence if the input reaches the rule.
  1900-02-29 is refused by the epoch guard whatever the leap rule says.
- Half a two-sided rule is not coverage of it. never_revoke_only,
  mx_was_secure, CtLogList::is_empty, the guarded insert -- all tested
  in one direction only.
- Determinism is not distinctness. The UUID seed tests asserted
  identical input gives identical output and never the converse, which a
  constant satisfies while giving every Finding the same UUID.

## Non-test findings filed

PKIX-z0hq  CRL cache rollback accepts any CRL lacking cRLNumber
PKIX-j81h  an expect() coupling two predicates with only a comment
PKIX-1zkq  sans-IO state machines: a deleted arm hangs, closed as
           accounted for
PKIX-zn4l  pkix-chain's const-block Send/Sync assertion, unobservable
PKIX-nabg  closed -- the producedAt boundary WAS testable, I was wrong

## Tooling corrections made during the campaign

- The test-module -E filter matters only where test modules hold helper
  functions; measured 549->541 on pkix-path, no change on pkix-ac or
  pkix-revocation-http. Check with a diff of the two listings, never a
  count.
- The -j limit is across the machine, not per sweep. Five concurrent
  runs gave 92% iowait and a twenty-to-one slowdown.
- A fixture the corpus lacks can still be built; two lints carried
  stale "requires fixture generation" notes hiding eleven mutants."}
